description: Looking to build an interactive Junior Astronaut Training experience with fun challenges and engaging simulations.
summary:
ASTRA-X: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive 3D simulation created with the Unity engine that combines aspects of overly simplified STEM games with realistic orbital engineering problems. It immerses users in a realistic world of space mission training with various modules including diagnostics of solar arrays, radiation levels checking, physical exercises, and pre-flight medical examinations.

In order to solve the problem, ASTRA-X translates difficult space mission engineering trade-offs into simple choices. Unlike conventional space education that teaches users to understand different systems separately, ASTRA-X helps students see how the competing factors like energy production and radiation protection, crew health and life support affect the outcome of the mission.

It is crucial because standard space engineering education is focused on passive learning through reading or math, which may be difficult for children to understand. By providing the possibility to interactively work with outpost consoles and see cause-and-effect relations in 3D environment, ASTRA-X develops skills of systems thinking and motivates future space explorers and engineers.
details:
HOW IT WORKS AND WHAT IT DOES

ASTRA-X: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, first-person 3D simulation allowing the user to become a space academy trainee getting ready for work at outposts on planets other than Earth. In the game, the player will move around the hub and different academy buildings, interacting with outpost consoles using raycast-based mechanics and diegetic user interface cues. The game has several modules such as solar array diagnostics, radiation level inspections, tests of physical stamina and reaction time, and pre-mission medical check-ups. In order to get a clearance for the mission, the player needs to balance various mission requirements (power, radiation shielding, life support load, and crew physiology).

ADVANTAGES AND IMPACT

Standard space-themed STEM teaching materials either dumb down engineering considerations or overload the reader with mathematical formulas. This product fills the need by converting complex systems engineering into practical gameplay based on cause-and-effect reasoning. The target impact of this product is the development of systems thinking among the learners.

Creative and Design Considerations

Diegetic Experience Beats Textbook Learning: Rather than offering only static quizzes, ASTRA-X integrates the trade-offs of engineering directly into the 3D, walkable environment and interactive diagnostic control panels to create an experience that feels like astronauts on duty.

Accessibility v. Realism: We ensured a careful balance between realism in physics (e.g., radiation levels, power levels of solar energy, biometrics), accessibility in controls (WASD, mouse look, keyboard actions), and visual cues to make the game accessible for young learners.

Modular Design: With our design approach, we have been able to compartmentalize each trade-off of engineering while also showing the importance of each subsystem to mission survival.

Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware

  • Game Engine & Pipeline: Unity 6 (Built-in 3D Render Pipeline)
  • Programming Language: C# (custom player controllers, raycast interaction systems, scene state managers, and UI controllers)
  • Development Environment & Version Control: Visual Studio Code, Git, Git LFS, and GitHub.
  • Hardware: Developed and tested on a Windows PC.
